say.never: A robot has only one shooter, so the whole program must share the same one. Two things make that happen. A `private` constructor means nobody else can write `new ShooterSubsystem()`. And `getInstance()` hands out the one copy, building it the first time it's asked.
say.bit: The whole robot must share **one** shooter. A private constructor stops anyone writing `new`, and `getInstance()` hands out the single copy.

say.never: `extends MwSubsystem` means "the shooter *is a* subsystem", so it gets everything a subsystem has for free. `@Override` marks the methods where the shooter fills in its own version.
say.bit: `extends MwSubsystem` gives the shooter everything a subsystem has. `@Override` marks the methods it fills in.
